statement: Let i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{L-1} be the indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] == -1, so L is the number of -1 entries in nums. The function returns a vector r with len(r) = L such that for every t with 0 <= t < L: let k be the number of indices j with 0 <= j <= i_t such that nums[q] == -1 for every q with j <= q <= i_t (the length of the maximal contiguous block of -1s ending at i_t), and let p_1 > p_2 > ... > p_m be the indices p with 0 <= p < i_t and nums[p] != -1, listed in strictly decreasing order (m is the number of such indices). If k <= m then r[t] = nums[p_k]; if k > m then r[t] = -1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Let L be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] == -1. The function returns a vector r with len(r) = L.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: For every t with 0 <= t < len(r), either r[t] == -1 or 1 <= r[t] <= 100.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail) for every nums satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: For every t with 0 <= t < len(r), if r[t] != -1, letting i_t be the t-th index (0-based) with nums[i_t] == -1, there exists an index p such that 0 <= p < i_t, nums[p] != -1, and r[t] = nums[p].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: For every t with 0 <= t < len(r), letting i_t be the t-th index with nums[i_t] == -1 and k the length of the maximal contiguous block of -1s ending at i_t, we have r[t] == -1 if and only if the number of indices p with 0 <= p < i_t and nums[p] != -1 is strictly less than k.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: For every t with 0 <= t < len(r) and r[t] != -1, letting i_t be the t-th index with nums[i_t] == -1, k the length of the maximal contiguous block of -1s ending at i_t, and p_1 > p_2 > ... > p_m the indices p with 0 <= p < i_t and nums[p] != -1 in strictly decreasing order (m = number of such indices), we have k <= m and r[t] = nums[p_k].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: For every t with 0 <= t < len(r), if i_t == 0 or nums[i_t - 1] != -1 (so the -1 at i_t starts a new maximal contiguous block of -1s), then: if there is at least one index p with 0 <= p < i_t and nums[p] != -1, r[t] = nums[p] where p is the largest such index; otherwise r[t] = -1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: For any t with 0 <= t < len(r) and r[t] != -1, define the source index of r[t] as the unique p such that 0 <= p < i_t, nums[p] = r[t], and the number of positive entries in nums[p+1 .. i_t-1] equals k(i_t) - 1, where i_t is the t-th -1 index and k(i_t) is the length of the maximal contiguous block of -1s ending at i_t. For every t with 0 <= t < len(r) - 1, if i_{t+1} = i_t + 1 and both r[t] != -1 and r[t+1] != -1, then the source index of r[t+1] is strictly less than the source index of r[t].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: For every t with 0 <= t < len(r), let i_t be the t-th index with nums[i_t] == -1. For any array nums' satisfying the preconditions and agreeing with nums on all indices j with 0 <= j <= i_t, the t-th element of the result computed from nums' equals r[t].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Let i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{L-1} be the indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] == -1. For every t with 0 <= t < L - 1, if i_{t+1} = i_t + 1 and r[t] == -1, then r[t+1] == -1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] == -1 or 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.
